messages:
Ivy: Noticed a weird interaction between adaptive routing (cost-based) and tenant quota checks. Hosted will reject when qps_limit reached and we fallback to dedicated, but quota check runs again and sometimes denies the request causing a double-fail path. Repro in staging.
Marco: Seen this too. Root cause: quota evaluation happens at the entrypoint before routing. If hosted rejects, control plane routes but doesn't re-evaluate quota against the target cluster's limits/pools.
Lena: That explains the double-deny. We need a clear semantic: is quota an admission control that is evaluated only once per-request, or should each target re-evaluate?
Chris: For Dedicated/Private the operators often have their own quota policies. We must re-evaluate after routing if the target enforces local quotas. Otherwise requests may be routed into a cluster and dropped.
Ivy: Proposed semantics: 
- Pre-route admission: does the request satisfy global account quotas? If no -> reject early.
- Post-route admission: target cluster applies local capacity checks (dedicated pool limits, tenant throttle). If target denies and fallback options remain, attempt other targets; otherwise return a clear 429 with reason.
Marco: Implementation detail: adapter currently assumes quota was a global pre-check and fails fast. Need to plumb a retryable-deny signal so control plane knows to try next candidate rather than synthesize a generic error.
Lena: We should extend the edge proto error taxonomy with codes: QUOTA_GLOBAL, QUOTA_TARGET_RETRYABLE, QUOTA_TARGET_FATAL. That allows smarter routing policies.
Chris: Also need to avoid quota double-counting. If pre-route decremented a token from a global quota and post-route denies, we must roll that token back or implement a reservation with TTL. Otherwise customers get charged/blocked incorrectly.
Ivy: Reservation idea: pre-route creates a short-lived reservation token that is only committed on successful target accept. Reservation TTL default 2s. If expired or released, quota is returned. Pseudocode: 
```text
pre_route: reserve = quota.reserve(account_id, amount, ttl=2000ms)
if reserve.failed -> QUOTA_GLOBAL
route -> target.accept(reserve_token)
if target.reject_retryable -> try next target (pass reserve_token)
if finally accepted -> quota.commit(reserve_token)
if all fail -> quota.release(reserve_token)
```
Marco: That seems reasonable but requires quota service to support reserve/commit/release primitives. Our current quota service is simple counters. We'll need to add reservation layer or emulate via optimistic increments with compensating ops.
Lena: Security/consistency: reservation tokens must be opaque and single-use. Also need audit trail: reserve_id, account_id, amount, timestamps.
Chris: Ops concern: reservations could be abused to hold capacity during high churn. Enforce small TTLs and rate-limit reserve attempts per account. Also instrument reservation saturation metrics.
ProductBot: Note created: QUA-301 "quota-reservation-and-target-retry-handshake" -> https://redwood/QUA-301
Ivy: One more: the routing DSL should expose a per-route fallback_quota_behavior: 
- prefer_reserve (try to hold quota while failing over)
- precheck_only (only global check, do not reserve)
- target_authoritative (defer entirely to target quotas)
Example: 
```yaml
routing_policy:
  fallback_quota_behavior: prefer_reserve
```
Marco: Backcompat: if quota service doesn't support reserve, adapters should use best-effort with idempotent compensating release. Document caveats in rollout notes.
Lena: Tests: correctness under concurrent failovers, reservation TTL expiry, reservation storms, and accounting reconciliation checks. Also billing needs to get a clear commit/release hook.
Chris: I'll add an infra task to prototype the reserve API and a stress test harness.
Ivy: I'll draft a short RFC addendum and a sequence diagram showing reserve->route->commit flow.
InfraBot: Created task INF-1302: "quota-reservation-prototype".
Marco: UX: Console should show reservation failures and a small explanation why a request was denied with links to remediation. DevEx can craft messaging.
Lena: We also need metric labels: reserve_attempted, reserve_committed, reserve_released, reserve_expired. Tag with route and account_hash.
Chris: Ok owners: Marco takes adapter changes, Ivy writes RFC, Lena owns quota service changes, I'll own stress tests. Can we sync in 30 to align interfaces?
Ivy: Works for me. Meeting invite incoming. :thumbsup:
